name: The Pop Group
label: Rough Trade
lede: Five Bristol teenagers wanted to be a pop group, hired a dub producer, shouted over free jazz and played their last show to half a million people in Trafalgar Square. They were finished barely out of their teens.

hero.by: The Pop Group in 2014. Wikimedia Commons

eras.title: A prefab youth club in Bristol
eras.text: The Pop Group came out of a postwar prefab youth club and Bristol's funk and reggae nights, where Mark Stewart was tall enough to get in at 12. Punk opened the door; they walked through it toward James Brown, Funkadelic, Albert Ayler and King Tubby instead of the Clash.

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group · Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: Three hours of "My Generation" on a borrowed-money guitar
years.p: Gareth Sager buys a guitar with money a girl lent him and the band jams [[The Who|9fdaa16b-a6c4-4831-b87c-bc9ca8ce7eaa]] for three hours. The next day, Stewart says, it's "I Wanna Be Your Dog".
years.xp:
Sager is firm on the date: "I hate it when people say we started in 1978! It was April '77."

The line-up: [[Mark Stewart|ae1a332b-b032-4edc-a1b6-9dc9f94fe3d3]] on vocals, Sager on guitar and sax, [[John Waddington|744f3e52-e9c5-4e80-be5a-b83a21c948b9]] on guitar, [[Simon Underwood|e9fc3473-f6ad-4392-8c0b-50c392c1542b]] on bass and [[Bruce Smith|bb92f697-681a-409f-a5c2-1e5e52520e07]] on drums. Stewart found Waddington in a band called the Boyfriends at a youth club down the road.

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: "We wanted to be a pop group"
years.p: Smith says the name came up in a van coming back from the Roxy and made them laugh for days. Stewart says it was his, his mum says it was hers, and he doesn't much mind.
years.xp: Stewart's version runs back to a band he dreamed up at 13 called the Wild Boys, after the Burroughs book, where everybody would come onstage out of dustbins. "I'm into plagiarism, myself," he told Rolling Stone. "It was obviously me, but you have to give other people credit."

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: The Stranglers' crowds go silent
years.p: Hugh Cornwell produces early demos and the band land support shows with the Stranglers. Smith: "it was like crickets when we finished."

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: Nico, Linton Kwesi Johnson and Cabaret Voltaire on one bill
years.p: The band headline their own show at Camden's Electric Ballroom. Johnny Thunders and the Heartbreakers play elsewhere the same night, and London has to pick a side.
years.xp:
Sager remembers it as a dividing line: "The people who'd moved on wanted to see us." Sets never ran past about 40 minutes.

Earlier that year, opening for [[Magazine|043324ca-100d-48ce-8c7c-fd015afc103b]], they played an eight-minute "We Are Fire". Sager: nobody in that scene had ever played an eight-minute song.

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: John Cale falls asleep at the first meeting
years.p: [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] was their first pick to produce the album. He came to Underwood's flea-ridden flat in Bristol straight off the plane and dozed off mid-conversation; the band dropped the idea.
years.xp: Their second choice didn't work out either. Stewart: "We tried to work with King Tubby, but he got shot."

eras.title: Dennis Bovell at the desk
eras.text: Radar, a Warner Bros. imprint flush with Elvis Costello money, paid for a debut that sounded like nothing on the label. Thatcher's election that spring turned the band's politics up, and by the end of the year they were on Rough Trade.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group · Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
yt: She Is Beyond Good and Evil
years.h: "She Is Beyond Good and Evil" is the first single
years.p: Released on Radar to acclaim. Decades later St. Vincent made it a regular on her Strange Mercy tour.

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: Dennis Bovell mixes Y like a dub record
years.p: The band chose Dennis Bovell for his dub of "Raindrops" and pushed him to play the desk as an instrument. Smith was 17.
years.xp:
Rolling Stone calls them the first rock group to let a dub producer run wild with their music. "We were all sitting, splicing tapes, and making the thing in the same room at the same time," Stewart said.

Smith on who paid: "Elvis Costello paid for us, it's that simple." Sager on how it went down at Radar: "It was horrible for Radar."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
yt: We Are Time, live at Glastonbury 1979
years.h: On the NME cover, and the tour money goes to Amnesty
years.p: The band give the proceeds of their first big tour to Amnesty International.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: Dan Catsis takes over bass from Simon Underwood
years.p: Underwood goes on to Pigbag; [[Dan Catsis|25a25cfa-218e-41e0-b48e-5fd79000877f]] plays on the Rough Trade records.

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group · Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: "We Are All Prostitutes" opens the Rough Trade years
years.p: Out of the Warner Bros. orbit and onto [[Rough Trade|4f4b0013-1704-4936-a769-e6e8a6e08ff8]]. Smith calls it the best recording the band ever made.
years.xp:
"The attraction of making our next records for Rough Trade was our consciences not being answerable to a multinational corporation," Smith told Rolling Stone. Sager says Thatcher's election that May politicised them almost overnight.

The cellist on the record is Tristan Honsinger, one of the free improvisers Sager had just discovered. A lost video shot at the Electric Ballroom in November 1979 resurfaced decades later from video artist Chris Reynolds' attic.

eras.title: Throw the chords out the window
eras.text: The second album was angrier and freer, and the band started pulling in opposite directions: Sager toward Sun Ra and Han Bennink, Stewart toward agitprop he could actually sing over. It ended at a CND rally, though nobody knew it was the end.

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
yt: Feed the Hungry, live at Alexandra Palace 1980
years.h: For How Much Longer Do We Tolerate Mass Murder? splits the room
years.p: Sager, fresh from seeing Sun Ra's big band, wants free improvisation. Stewart can't put words over tracks like "Communicate", and Smith feels it turning into Stewart's band.
years.xp:
"It began to feel less like a band and more like Mark saying, 'It's going to be like this,'" Smith told Rolling Stone.

Stewart's side: "I'm not a musician. I can't stand on one leg and improvise like the guy from Can."

years.cap: The Pop Group at Alexandra Palace, London, June 15, 1980
years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group · Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: A split single with the Slits
years.p: "Where There's a Will..." pairs the band with [[The Slits|ff9ef2ef-73a6-496c-8528-4b12b21afbfd]], who share their drummer Bruce Smith and their manager Dick O'Dell. The We Are Time collection follows.

years.cap: The CND rally in Trafalgar Square, 1980
years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group · Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: The last show is for half a million people at a CND rally
years.p: Stewart, volunteering in the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament office, talks Monsignor Bruce Kent into adding music. The band end with William Blake's "Jerusalem" over rasta rhythms in Trafalgar Square.
years.xp: Stewart also roped in [[Killing Joke|f5aca88c-e3c1-4bc2-af33-68a9a9f7b56a]]. "We weren't aware that it would be the last Pop Group gig," he said. "So I started my new stuff on the same day the Pop Group ended."

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group · Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: Legal wrangling and arguments end the band
years.p: Sager: "The group had basically run its course." Smith, on Stewart: "This is what I'm going to do and you're either in or you're not."

years.src: Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group · Wikipedia: The Pop Group · Wikipedia: Mark Stewart
years.h: Rip Rig + Panic, Maximum Joy, Pigbag, New Age Steppers
years.p: Sager and Smith start Rip Rig + Panic with Sean Oliver and, before long, Neneh Cherry. Stewart heads to Adrian Sherwood's On-U Sound circle and the New Age Steppers.

years.src: Wikipedia: Mark Stewart
years.h: Mark Stewart & the Maffia cope with cowardice
years.p: Stewart's first album after the band, Learning to Cope with Cowardice, comes out of the On-U crew. Later records go through Mute Records and collaborators from [[Massive Attack|10adbe5e-a2c0-4bf3-8249-2b4cbf6e6ca8]] to Trent Reznor.

eras.title: Blame The Simpsons
eras.text: Matt Groening's invitation to an All Tomorrow's Parties he was curating got four of them talking again. The reunion ran to two new albums, a world tour and a full reissue programme before Stewart's death in 2023.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group · Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: Matt Groening asks for a Pop Group reunion
years.p: The Simpsons creator invites the band to his ATP. Stewart, Sager, Smith and Catsis come back; Waddington doesn't.
years.xp: "I blame The Simpsons for getting [the Pop Group] back together," Stewart told Rolling Stone, adding that the ATP set itself didn't happen but the call kickstarted everything.

years.cap: The Pop Group in Los Angeles
years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group · Rolling Stone: The Oral History of the Pop Group
years.h: We Are Time returns, with a Cabinet of Curiosities
years.p: The band's own label, Freaks R Us, reissues the 1980 collection worldwide alongside a new rarities set, and the band tour the UK for a week.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: Citizen Zombie, 35 years after the last one
years.p: Produced by Paul Epworth, the first Pop Group studio album since 1980 sends them out on a world tour.

years.cap: Mark Stewart in Los Angeles, March 10, 2015
years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: Stewart in Los Angeles on the Citizen Zombie tour
years.p: The world tour runs through the US, Japan and Australia, then Europe, finishing with two sets at Glastonbury.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: Dennis Bovell is back for Honeymoon on Mars
years.p: The Y producer returns for the fourth studio album, recorded through 2016.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: Mute reissues Y, and Bovell redubs it
years.p: The debut comes back with unreleased live and studio tracks; Y in Dub, a new Bovell treatment, follows in 2021.

years.src: NME: The Pop Group's Mark Stewart dies aged 62 · Wikipedia: Mark Stewart
years.h: Mark Stewart dies at 62
years.p: The band announced it; no cause of death was given. [[Massive Attack|10adbe5e-a2c0-4bf3-8249-2b4cbf6e6ca8]] called him a post-punk pioneer and Geoff Barrow called him the Godfather of Bristol.
years.xp:
Steve Albini, Adrian Sherwood and Sleaford Mods were among the others paying tribute. Sherwood called Stewart "the biggest musical influence in my life."

A final solo album, The Fateful Symmetry, came out on Mute in 2025.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Pop Group
years.h: John Waddington dies at 63
years.p: The founding guitarist's death is announced two months after Stewart's.
